title: Dirac method descriptor
description: The API identity of one compute method: what it accepts, what it returns, what it refuses, how it executes, and where it is exposed. THIS FILE IS THE AUTHORITY, not the database. meta.method in PostgreSQL is a registered historical SNAPSHOT of a descriptor; the runtime catalog loads descriptors from git. Reasons the DB cannot be the root: it may be unreachable, SDK generation happens at build time, MCP tool discovery needs a stable snapshot, historical contracts belong in version control, and meta.register_method() returns an existing row when method_id+version match WITHOUT comparing schemas — so a descriptor change under an unchanged implementation digest would silently keep the old schema.

method_id.description: Dotted, stable, and part of the public API. Renaming one is a breaking change.

implementation.description: How the IMPLEMENTATION digest is computed. Deliberately separate from this descriptor's own digest: changing a summary or an MCP wording must not invalidate a cached cube, and changing a basis set or a grid constant must. Those are different questions and one hash cannot answer both.

constants.description: Module-level constants the functions READ. Omitting these is how 22 cached cubes were served with stale geometry after a padding constant changed and no version moved.

schema.$comment: A JSON Schema. additionalProperties:false is required at the top level so a misspelled field fails at the boundary rather than being silently ignored.

artifacts.description: Artifact ROLES this method may produce. A large result is referenced, never inlined (ADR-003).

refusals.description: What this method REFUSES, as first-class data rather than as prose in an error string. An agent choosing between methods needs to know the refusal before it spends a budget.

measured.description: The measurement that justifies the refusal, where one exists.

warnings.description: Scope limits this method may attach to a SUCCESSFUL result. Separate from refusals because the result exists — an agent must distinguish 'refused', 'returned but scope-limited' and 'fully supported'.

execution.description: Replaces the binary exec_class: interactive|job, which could not describe a method whose cost spans a second to an hour on the same code path.

concurrency_class.description: Methods sharing a concurrency_class share an admission bound. 'scf' is bounded at 2 on this box, derived from pyscf's 4000 MB per-SCF planning budget against the 8 GB the unit reserves.

exposure.description: Not every method should become an agent tool. 400 MCP tools destroy tool selection, so MCP exposure is curated per method.

invocation.description: What makes this descriptor EXECUTABLE rather than merely descriptive. Without it a catalog can list, validate and document a method and cannot run one — which is exactly the gap the external audit named 'agent-compatible, not agent-native'. The handler is a STRING, resolved lazily by importlib, so a CLI can list every method and estimate its cost without importing pyscf.

estimate.description: module:callable returning a cost prediction BEFORE running. The reason a budget refusal can be issued in milliseconds instead of after ninety seconds of SCF.

artifacts.description: The roles this method produces. Declared so a client knows what references to expect before it calls, and so a missing artifact is a contract violation rather than an empty list.
